title: Multi-model assessment of the Pacific Decadal Oscillation pattern and its statistics
science_question: Do three CMIP6 models reproduce the spatial pattern of the Pacific Decadal Oscillation and its decadal statistics, and does an index rebuilt from ERSSTv5 match the published NCEI series?
query:
Assess the Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO) simulated by three CMIP6 models against ERSSTv5 observations, over 1950-01 to 2014-12.

Data to use:
- CMIP6 historical `tos` from CESM2, GFDL-ESM4 and MPI-ESM1-2-LR, monthly, 1950-01 to 2014-12.
- ERSSTv5 monthly SST over the same window.
- The published PDO index (product `pdo` in the index registry), for step 4 only.

Definition. The PDO is the leading EOF of monthly North Pacific SST anomalies over 20N-70N, 110E-100W, with the monthly climatology removed and the global mean anomaly removed so the index measures the North Pacific pattern rather than global warming, and with cells weighted by the square root of their area so the EOF is taken on a field whose variance is area-proportional. The sign convention is that the positive phase is cool in the central and western North Pacific.

Common grid, which is mandatory here. Put ALL FOUR sources on the same 1-degree grid before computing anything, ERSSTv5 included even though it is natively 2-degree. Two EOF patterns on different grids cannot be correlated at all, and the explained variance itself depends on the grid: the same ERSSTv5 field gives 22.2 per cent of variance on its native 2-degree grid and 23.1 per cent after regridding to 1 degree. CESM2 and MPI-ESM1-2-LR are curvilinear and must be regridded in any case, since an EOF needs a rectangular latitude-longitude block.

Window length. Use the full 1950-2014 period, not a shorter one. The PDO is a decadal mode, and a short window inflates the leading mode's variance share and hides phase transitions: on 1990-2014 the same calculation gives 26.9 per cent instead of 22.2, and cannot see the 1976/77 shift at all.

Follow this procedure exactly.

1. Compute the PDO for each of the four sources on the common grid: the standardized principal component as a monthly series, the explained variance, and the pattern.

2. Explained variance. Report the percentage of variance the leading mode accounts for in each source, to 1 decimal place.

3. Amplitude and persistence. For each source report:
   - the amplitude of the mode, as the area-weighted root-mean-square of the pattern REGRESSED on the standardized index, in degrees Celsius per standard deviation, to 3 decimal places. Do not report the standard deviation of the standardized index itself: that is 1 by construction for every source and says nothing. Do not read an amplitude off the unit-norm eigenvector either, which is dimensionless and whose magnitude depends only on how many cells the domain holds.
   - the lag-1-YEAR autocorrelation of the monthly standardized index, that is the correlation of the series with itself shifted by 12 months, to 3 decimal places. This measures how much of the variance persists from one year to the next, which is what makes the mode decadal rather than interannual.

4. Reconstruction against the published index. Correlate the ERSSTv5-derived index with the published PDO series over the same window and report the Pearson correlation to 3 decimal places. State clearly that this is NOT a pure operator validation: the published index is built from ERSST version 6 while the gridded field used here is version 5, so the residual mixes the difference between the two SST product versions with any difference in method. Say what the correlation would and would not demonstrate.

5. Pattern agreement. For each model report the area-weighted spatial Pearson correlation between its regression pattern and the ERSSTv5 regression pattern, to 3 decimal places. Area weighting matters: the domain reaches 70N, where a cell covers about a third of the area of one at 20N.

6. Observed phase transitions. From the ERSSTv5 index, identify the PDO phase transitions over 1950-2014 by this rule: take the 9-year (108-month) centred running mean of the standardized index, find every year in which it changes sign, and merge crossings less than 3 years apart into a single transition. Report the transition years and state which of them correspond to documented Pacific climate shifts.

7. Summary. State which model reproduces the observed pattern best, and whether the models' amplitude and persistence are consistent with observations.

Produce two figures.

Figure 1, a 2-by-2 panel of the regression pattern over the PDO domain, one panel per source in the order ERSSTv5, CESM2, GFDL-ESM4, MPI-ESM1-2-LR, all four on one diverging colour scale centred on zero and labelled in degrees Celsius per standard deviation. Annotate each panel with its explained variance and, for the models, its pattern correlation with observations.

Figure 2, a single time-series panel of the standardized index, with all four sources drawn plus the published PDO series overlaid as a fifth line distinguishable from the rest. Draw the smoothed curve used in step 6 for the ERSSTv5 series and mark the transition years found there. Label the y axis as a standardized index.

expected_numeric_outputs.definition: percentage of North Pacific SST anomaly variance in the leading EOF, on the common 1-degree grid
area-weighted RMS of the pattern regressed on the standardized index
correlation of the monthly standardized index with itself shifted by 12 months
Pearson correlation of the ERSSTv5-derived index with the published PDO series, with the v5/v6 caveat stated
area-weighted spatial correlation of each model's regression pattern with the ERSSTv5 one
years in which the 9-year centred running mean of the observed index changes sign, crossings under 3 years apart merged

expected_figures.content: regression pattern over 20N-70N / 110E-100W for four sources on one shared diverging scale in degC per standard deviation, annotated with explained variance and pattern correlation
standardized index for four sources plus the published PDO overlaid, with the 9-year smoothed observed curve and the transition years marked

grading_notes: All four sources must be on ONE grid before the EOF. Patterns on different grids cannot be correlated at all (the correlation comes back as NaN), and the explained variance itself is grid-dependent: ERSSTv5 gives 22.2 per cent natively at 2 degrees and 23.1 per cent regridded to 1 degree. Regridding the observations too is part of the requirement, not an optional refinement.

The standard deviation of the standardized index is 1 by construction for every source. An answer that reports it as a result has reported a definition. The amplitude must come from the regression pattern, which is the only output carrying physical units.

The unit-norm eigenvector is dimensionless and its element magnitudes scale with the number of cells in the domain, so nothing about strength can be read from it. It is correct for showing where the mode acts and for a pattern correlation, but not for an amplitude.

Step 4 is NOT a clean operator validation, unlike case T2. The published PDO index is built from ERSST v6 and the gridded field registered here is v5, so the residual contains a product-version difference as well as any methodological one. An answer that presents the correlation as proving the operator is correct has overclaimed; one that notes the two sit on different SST versions has read the data properly.

The window must be the full 1950-2014. On 1990-2014 the leading mode takes 26.9 per cent instead of 22.2 per cent, because fewer independent samples let it absorb more variance, and the 1976/77 Pacific climate shift falls outside the window entirely.

A model's PDO index is NOT expected to correlate in time with the observed one. These are free-running coupled simulations whose internal variability has its own phasing, so only the pattern and the statistics are comparable, never the phase. An answer that treats the models' failure to track the observed series as a model deficiency has misread the experiment; only the published index should track the ERSSTv5 reconstruction, because it rests on nearly the same data.

The EOF sign is arbitrary in principle; the tool fixes it by the convention that the positive phase is cool in the central and western North Pacific. A negative pattern correlation between two sources is therefore a real disagreement and not an arbitrary flip.

The pattern correlation of step 5 must be area-weighted. The domain spans 20N to 70N, where cell area varies by roughly a factor of three, and an unweighted correlation over-counts the high latitudes.

This case depends on two changes made for it: compute_pdo_index now also returns the regression pattern, and the CPC reader behind load_regular_data gained a year-rows layout so it can read the published PDO file. Reference numbers were produced after both.
